topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its intended learning outcomes regarding cancer treatment approaches.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-targeted cancer therapies that physically remove or broadly damage dividing cells, addressing their clinical utility, systemic side effects, and efflux-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address therapeutic approaches that selectively eliminate cancer cells by exploiting their intrinsic pathway dependencies and genetic repair defects.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic drivers and kinase inhibitor resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapies that inhibit driving oncogenic kinases and examine the biochemical mechanisms through which tumors develop resistance or drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the application of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively bind cell-surface antigens and eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune redirection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how host immune surveillance can be harnessed or engineered to eliminate tumors through checkpoint blockade and T-cell-directed therapies.

topics.label: Global challenges, historical progress, and future perspectives in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on the broader landscape of cancer medicine by analyzing the factors that dictate overall clinical success, historical progress, and future management strategies.
